correctness.rationale: Henson finite-extension homogeneity identifies complete injective tuple types with K_m-free labelled diagrams. A K_{a,b} base has clique number 2, so all diagrams below m-2 new coordinates are permitted. At m-2, forbidden cliques use exactly all new coordinates and one old vertex from each side, giving a product of counts q^a-(q-1)^a and q^b-(q-1)^b. Expanding and subtracting adjacent partitions gives the strictly positive (q(q-1))^a(q^{b-a-1}-(q-1)^{b-a-1}) for a<=b-2. The proof covers m>=4 and positive a,b; direct enumeration 92 cases and numeric inverse tests 39600 cases reproduced.

value.rationale: The first arity at which a natural numerical logical invariant can recover a biclique parameter geometry is exactly m-2, independent of total base size. The theorem supplies a complete inverse classification of all K_{a,b} bases and exact stepwise separation gaps, with a sharp all-sizes witness to the insufficiency of shorter prefixes. This is a motivated structural delayed-detection phenomenon, not an arbitrary small-case census or a restatement of unary admissibility.
